title: The Case of the Short Cash Box
story: At the holiday craft fair on the Saturday after Thanksgiving, the cash box came up exactly twenty dollars short, and Hattie has added "find twenty dollars" to her list of lists. Nobody suspects a thief, only a slip of the fingers: the box sat on the cocoa table all day, and only the cocoa volunteer made change from it. Five volunteers each ran a different table for a different number of hours. Who made the wrong change?

texts: The volunteer with the holly name tag worked a shorter shift than the volunteer who sold mittens.
The volunteer who sold mittens wore either the pinecone or the reindeer name tag.
The volunteer who sold candles wore either the reindeer or the holly name tag.
Of Dev and the volunteer who sold cocoa, one wore the star name tag and the other wore the reindeer name tag.
The volunteer who worked 5 hours sold either wreaths or fudge.
Ruben worked a shorter shift than the volunteer who sold wreaths.
The volunteer with the holly name tag worked neither 2 hours nor 4 hours.
Of the volunteer who sold fudge and the volunteer who worked 3 hours, one is Una and the other is Elsa.
The five volunteers were the volunteer who worked 2 hours, Una, the volunteer who worked 5 hours, the volunteer with the star name tag, and the volunteer who worked 3 hours.
